authors: Maheshwari K, Nathanson BH, Munson SH, Khangulov V, Stevens M, Badani H, et al.
title: The relationship between ICU hypotension and in-hospital mortality and morbidity in septic patients
what_it_supports: In 8,782 septic ICU patients from 110 US hospitals, greater time-weighted MAP below 65 mmHg was associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality, AKI and myocardial injury.
abstract_snippet: "For every one unit increase in TWA-MAP < 65 mmHg, the odds of in-hospital mortality increased 11.4% (95% CI 7.8%, 15.1%, p < 0.001); the odds of AKI increased 7.0%"

authors: Vincent JL, Nielsen ND, Shapiro NI, Gerbasi ME, Grossman A, Doroff R, et al.
title: Mean arterial pressure and mortality in patients with distributive shock: a retrospective analysis of the MIMIC-III database
what_it_supports: In MIMIC-III distributive shock, longer episodes of MAP below 65 mmHg were associated with higher ICU mortality (observational).
abstract_snippet: "compared to patients in whom MAP was never < 65 mmHg, ICU mortality increased as duration of hypotension < 65 mmHg increased"

authors: Khanna AK, Maheshwari K, Mao G, Liu L, Perez-Protto SE, Chodavarapu P, et al.
title: Association Between Mean Arterial Pressure and Acute Kidney Injury and a Composite of Myocardial Injury and Mortality in Postoperative Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis
what_it_supports: In postoperative surgical ICU patients, lower daily minimum MAP was associated with myocardial injury/mortality and AKI (observational).
abstract_snippet: "Increasing amounts of hypotension (defined by lowest mean arterial pressures per day) were strongly associated with myocardial injury, mortality, and renal injury in postoperative critical care patients."

authors: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, Antonelli M, Coopersmith CM, French C, et al.
title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021
verified_via: Crossref + PubMed + OpenAlex (PMID 34605781); snippet from guideline full text (PMC8486643, ICM version; identical recommendation); checked 2026-11-23
what_it_supports: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 recommends an initial MAP target of 65 mmHg for adults with septic shock on vasopressors (Recommendation 9; CCM version).
abstract_snippet: "For adults with septic shock on vasopressors, we recommend an initial target mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 65 mm Hg over higher MAP targets"

authors: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, Antonelli M, Coopersmith CM, French C, et al.
title: Surviving sepsis campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021
verified_via: Crossref + PubMed + OpenAlex (PMID 34599691); snippet from full text PMC8486643 (no PubMed abstract); checked 2026-11-23
what_it_supports: Same guideline, Intensive Care Medicine version; Recommendation 9 sets an initial MAP target of 65 mmHg in septic shock.
abstract_snippet: "For adults with septic shock on vasopressors, we recommend an initial target mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 65 mm Hg over higher MAP targets"

authors: Asfar P, Meziani F, Hamel JF, Grelon F, Megarbane B, Anguel N, et al.
title: High versus Low Blood-Pressure Target in Patients with Septic Shock
what_it_supports: RCT (SEPSISPAM): targeting MAP 80-85 vs 65-70 mmHg in septic shock did not change 28- or 90-day mortality.
abstract_snippet: "At 28 days, there was no significant between-group difference in mortality, with deaths reported in 142 of 388 patients in the high-target group (36.6%) and 132 of 388 patients in the low-target group (34.0%)"

authors: Lamontagne F, Richards-Belle A, Thomas K, Harrison DA, Sadique MZ, Grieve RD, et al.
title: Effect of Reduced Exposure to Vasopressors on 90-Day Mortality in Older Critically Ill Patients With Vasodilatory Hypotension
what_it_supports: RCT (65 trial): permissive hypotension (MAP 60-65 mmHg) in ICU patients aged >=65 reduced vasopressor exposure without a significant 90-day mortality difference; supports 65 mmHg as a clinically relevant floor.
abstract_snippet: "To determine whether reducing exposure to vasopressors through permissive hypotension (mean arterial pressure [MAP] target, 60-65 mm Hg) reduces mortality at 90 days"

authors: Walsh M, Devereaux PJ, Garg AX, Kurz A, Turan A, Rodseth RN, et al.
title: Relationship between Intraoperative Mean Arterial Pressure and Clinical Outcomes after Noncardiac Surgery
what_it_supports: In 33,330 noncardiac surgeries, intraoperative MAP below 55 mmHg was associated with graded increases in AKI and myocardial injury with duration.
abstract_snippet: "The MAP threshold where the risk for both outcomes increased was less than 55 mmHg."

authors: Salmasi V, Maheshwari K, Yang D, Mascha EJ, Singh A, Sessler DI, et al.
title: Relationship between Intraoperative Hypotension, Defined by Either Reduction from Baseline or Absolute Thresholds, and Acute Kidney and Myocardial Injury after Noncardiac Surgery
what_it_supports: Intraoperative MAP below absolute 65 mmHg or 20% relative reduction was progressively associated with myocardial and kidney injury.
abstract_snippet: "MAP below absolute thresholds of 65 mmHg or relative thresholds of 20% were progressively related to both myocardial and kidney injury."

authors: Wesselink E, Kappen T, Torn H, Slooter A, van Klei W
title: Intraoperative hypotension and the risk of postoperative adverse outcomes: a systematic review
what_it_supports: Systematic review (42 articles): intraoperative hypotension is associated with end-organ injury, with risk rising with duration below 65-60 mmHg.
abstract_snippet: "Reported risks increase with increased durations for mean arterial pressures <65-60 mm Hg or for any exposure <55-50 mm Hg."

authors: Sendelbach S, Funk M
title: Alarm Fatigue
what_it_supports: Narrative review: most clinical alarms are false and alarm fatigue causes desensitisation and missed alarms.
abstract_snippet: "Research has demonstrated that 72% to 99% of clinical alarms are false. The high number of false alarms has led to alarm fatigue."

authors: Cvach M
title: Monitor Alarm Fatigue : An Integrative Review
what_it_supports: Integrative review of 72 articles on monitor alarm fatigue, linking it to high false-alarm rates and poor positive predictive value.
abstract_snippet: "The problem of alarm desensitization is multifaceted and related to a high false alarm rate, poor positive predictive value, lack of alarm standardization"

authors: Drew BJ, Harris P, Zègre-Hemsey JK, Mammone T, Schindler D, Salas-Boni R, et al.
title: Insights into the Problem of Alarm Fatigue with Physiologic Monitor Devices: A Comprehensive Observational Study of Consecutive Intensive Care Unit Patients
what_it_supports: In 461 ICU adults over 31 days, monitors generated 187 audible alarms per bed per day and 88.8% of annotated arrhythmia alarms were false.
abstract_snippet: "There were 381,560 audible alarms for an audible alarm burden of 187/bed/day. 88.8% of the 12,671 annotated arrhythmia alarms were false positives."

authors: Wijnberge M, Geerts BF, Hol L, Lemmers N, Mulder MP, Berge P, et al.
title: Effect of a Machine Learning–Derived Early Warning System for Intraoperative Hypotension vs Standard Care on Depth and Duration of Intraoperative Hypotension During Elective Noncardiac Surgery
what_it_supports: HYPE RCT (n=68): an ML early-warning system (HPI) with a treatment protocol reduced time-weighted intraoperative hypotension vs standard care.
abstract_snippet: "the use of a machine learning-derived early warning system compared with standard care resulted in less intraoperative hypotension"

authors: Maheshwari K, Shimada T, Yang D, Khanna S, Cywinski JB, Irefin SA, et al.
title: Hypotension Prediction Index for Prevention of Hypotension during Moderate- to High-risk Noncardiac Surgery
what_it_supports: RCT (n=214): HPI guidance did not reduce intraoperative hypotension; half of alerts were not followed by treatment. Note: published in Anesthesiology, not BJA.
abstract_snippet: "Index guidance therefore did not reduce amount of hypotension less than 65 mmHg, nor did it reduce hypotension less than 60 or 55 mmHg."

authors: Hatib F, Jian Z, Buddi S, Lee C, Settels J, Sibert K, et al.
title: Machine-learning Algorithm to Predict Hypotension Based on High-fidelity Arterial Pressure Waveform Analysis
what_it_supports: Original HPI development: ML on arterial waveform features predicted MAP<65 mmHg 5-15 min ahead with AUC 0.95-0.97 (case-control style selection).
abstract_snippet: "the algorithm predicted arterial hypotension with a sensitivity and specificity of 88% (85 to 90%) and 87% (85 to 90%) 15 min before a hypotensive event"

authors: Davies SJ, Vistisen ST, Jian Z, Hatib F, Scheeren TWL
title: Ability of an Arterial Waveform Analysis–Derived Hypotension Prediction Index to Predict Future Hypotensive Events in Surgical Patients
what_it_supports: Two-centre retrospective validation reporting HPI superior to MAP and delta-MAP for predicting IOH.
abstract_snippet: "The Hypotension Prediction Index performed superior to all other measured hemodynamic variables including mean arterial pressure and change in mean arterial pressure over a 3-minute window."

authors: Enevoldsen J, Vistisen ST
title: Performance of the Hypotension Prediction Index May Be Overestimated Due to Selection Bias
what_it_supports: Argues HPI training/validation selection makes MAP<75 always predict hypotension, so reported performance is overestimated by selection bias.
abstract_snippet: "We hypothesize that the data selection process introduced a systematic bias that resulted in an overestimation of the current MAP value's ability to predict future hypotension."

authors: Mulder MP, Harmannij-Markusse M, Fresiello L, Donker DW, Potters JW
title: Hypotension Prediction Index Is Equally Effective in Predicting Intraoperative Hypotension during Noncardiac Surgery Compared to a Mean Arterial Pressure Threshold: A Prospective Observational Study
what_it_supports: In 100 patients, HPI alarms matched a MAP threshold of 72-73 mmHg and HPI and concurrent MAP had near-identical AUROC.
abstract_snippet: "The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of the Hypotension Prediction Index (0.89 [0.88 to 0.89]) and concurrent mean arterial pressure (0.88 [0.88 to 0.89]) were almost identical"

authors: Yang HL, Celi LA, Lee H, Park SA, Lee S, Jung CW, et al.
title: The effect of selection bias on the performance of a deep learning-based intraoperative hypotension prediction model using real-world samples from a publicly available database
what_it_supports: On VitalDB, unbiased (all-sample) testing greatly increased alarms per hour and lowered PPV; DL beat a MAP-only model statistically but not clinically meaningfully.
abstract_snippet: "Although the DL model statistically performed better than the MAP-only model, the difference between the two models was not clinically meaningful."

authors: Florax AA, Mulder MP, van Ieperen RP, Fresiello L, Donker DW, Potters JW
title: Hypotension Prediction Index versus Mean Arterial Pressure Alarm for Preventing Intraoperative Hypotension in Elective Noncardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
what_it_supports: RCT (n=143): a MAP<72 mmHg alarm was noninferior to the HPI>85 alarm for preventing intraoperative hypotension.
abstract_snippet: "A mean arterial pressure alarm of 72 mmHg is noninferior to the Hypotension Prediction Index greater than 85 in preventing intraoperative hypotension."

authors: Hyland SL, Faltys M, Hüser M, Lyu X, Gumbsch T, Esteban C, et al.
title: Early prediction of circulatory failure in the intensive care unit using machine learning
what_it_supports: ICU circulatory-failure early warning with ML: 90% of events detected at about 0.05 alarms per patient-hour; precedent for alarm-burden reporting.
abstract_snippet: "It predicts 90% of circulatory-failure events in the test set, with 82% identified more than 2 h in advance"

authors: Yoon JH, Jeanselme V, Dubrawski A, Hravnak M, Pinsky MR, Clermont G
title: Prediction of hypotension events with physiologic vital sign signatures in the intensive care unit
what_it_supports: ICU ML model for the initial (first) hypotension event in MIMIC-III; alerts with lockout reached 0.79 alerts/subject/hour at 92.4% sensitivity.
abstract_snippet: "We developed a machine learning model to predict the initial hypotension event among intensive care unit (ICU) patients and designed an alert system for bedside implementation."

authors: Johnson AE, Pollard TJ, Shen L, Lehman LwH, Feng M, Ghassemi M, et al.
title: MIMIC-III, a freely accessible critical care database
what_it_supports: Describes MIMIC-III, a freely accessible single-centre critical care database (source cohort for the matched waveform/numerics subset).
abstract_snippet: "MIMIC-III ('Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care') is a large, single-center database comprising information relating to patients admitted to critical care units at a large tertiary care hospital."

authors: Goldberger AL, Amaral LAN, Glass L, Hausdorff JM, Ivanov PC, Mark RG, et al.
title: PhysioBank, PhysioToolkit, and PhysioNet
what_it_supports: Standard citation for PhysioNet/PhysioBank, the host of the MIMIC-III Waveform Database and eICU demo.
abstract_snippet: "PhysioBank is a large and growing archive of well-characterized digital recordings of physiological signals and related data for use by the biomedical research community."

authors: Moody B, Moody G, Villarroel M, Clifford G, Silva I
title: MIMIC-III Waveform Database Matched Subset (version 1.0)
verified_via: DataCite API; snippet from DataCite dataset description; checked 2026-11-23
what_it_supports: Dataset citation for the MIMIC-III Waveform Database Matched Subset v1.0 (numerics records with 1-min vitals incl. mean BP).
abstract_snippet: "The MIMIC-III Waveform Database Matched Subset contains 22,317 waveform records, and 22,247 numerics records, for 10,282 distinct ICU patients."

authors: Pollard TJ, Johnson AEW, Raffa JD, Celi LA, Mark RG, Badawi O
title: The eICU Collaborative Research Database, a freely available multi-center database for critical care research
what_it_supports: Describes the eICU Collaborative Research Database (multi-centre US ICU data, >200,000 admissions).
abstract_snippet: "Here we describe the eICU Collaborative Research Database, a multi-center intensive care unit (ICU)database with high granularity data for over 200,000 admissions"

authors: Johnson A, Pollard T, Badawi O, Raffa J
title: eICU Collaborative Research Database Demo (version 2.0.1)
verified_via: DataCite API; snippet from DataCite dataset description; checked 2026-11-23
what_it_supports: Dataset citation for the open eICU-CRD Demo v2.0.1 used in this study.
abstract_snippet: "This project is a demo version of the eICU Collaborative Research Database, a multi-center database comprised of deidentified health data for over 200,000 admissions to ICUs"

authors: Lee HC, Park Y, Yoon SB, Yang SM, Park D, Jung CW
title: VitalDB, a high-fidelity multi-parameter vital signs database in surgical patients
what_it_supports: Describes VitalDB, an open high-resolution intraoperative vital-sign dataset of 6,388 surgical cases.
abstract_snippet: "This dataset contains high-resolution multi-parameter data from 6,388 cases, including 486,451 waveform and numeric data tracks of 196 intraoperative monitoring parameters"

authors: Collins GS, Moons KGM, Dhiman P, Riley RD, Beam AL, Van Calster B, et al.
title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
what_it_supports: TRIPOD+AI reporting guideline (27-item checklist) for prediction model studies using regression or ML.
abstract_snippet: "TRIPOD+AI provides harmonised guidance for reporting prediction model studies, irrespective of whether regression modelling or machine learning methods have been used."

authors: Geirhos R, Jacobsen JH, Michaelis C, Zemel R, Brendel W, Bethge M, et al.
title: Shortcut learning in deep neural networks
verified_via: Crossref + OpenAlex; snippet from arXiv:2004.07780 abstract (same paper; Crossref/OpenAlex carry no abstract); checked 2026-11-23
what_it_supports: Defines shortcut learning: decision rules that perform well on standard benchmarks but fail to transfer to more challenging test conditions.
abstract_snippet: "Shortcuts are decision rules that perform well on standard benchmarks but fail to transfer to more challenging testing conditions, such as real-world scenarios."

authors: DeLong ER, DeLong DM, Clarke-Pearson DL
title: Comparing the Areas under Two or More Correlated Receiver Operating Characteristic Curves: A Nonparametric Approach
verified_via: Crossref + OpenAlex + PubMed (PMID 3203132); PubMed 3203132 (no DOI in PubMed record); checked 2026-11-23
what_it_supports: Nonparametric method for comparing correlated AUROCs from tests on the same individuals.
abstract_snippet: "When two or more empirical curves are constructed based on tests performed on the same individuals, statistical analysis on differences between curves must take into account the correlated nature of the data."

authors: Efron B
title: Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
what_it_supports: Introduces the bootstrap for estimating sampling distributions (basis for patient-level cluster bootstrap CIs).
abstract_snippet: "A general method, called the "bootstrap," is introduced, and shown to work satisfactorily on a variety of estimation problems."

authors: Romero-Brufau S, Huddleston JM, Escobar GJ, Liebow M
title: Why the C-statistic is not informative to evaluate early warning scores and what metrics to use
what_it_supports: Argues AUROC is uninformative for early warning scores and recommends sensitivity plus PPV/number needed to evaluate or alert rate.
abstract_snippet: "We suggest that pre-implementation evaluation of EWSs should include at least two metrics: sensitivity; and either the positive predictive value, number needed to evaluate, or estimated rate of alerts."

authors: Kamran F, Tjandra D, Heiler A, Virzi J, Singh K, King JE, et al.
title: Evaluation of Sepsis Prediction Models before Onset of Treatment
what_it_supports: Epic Sepsis Model AUROC fell from 0.62 to 0.47 when predictions made after clinical recognition were excluded: models can score well on already-recognised patients.
abstract_snippet: "When excluding predictions after clinical recognition, the AUROC dropped to 0.47 (95% CI, 0.46 to 0.48)."

authors: Wong A, Otles E, Donnelly JP, Krumm A, McCullough J, DeTroyer-Cooley O, et al.
title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
what_it_supports: External validation of the Epic Sepsis Model: poor discrimination (AUROC 0.63), large alert burden and few additional patients identified beyond usual care.
abstract_snippet: "The ESM also did not identify 1709 patients with sepsis (67%) despite generating alerts for an ESM score of 6 or higher for 6971 of all 38 455 hospitalized patients (18%)"

authors: Kim S, Ryu J, Kim S, Kim SH, Kim M, Yoon HJ
title: Intra-Session recurrence in intradialytic hypotension prediction: evaluation implications and recurrence-aware modeling
what_it_supports: Closest prior art: in dialysis, pooled IDH evaluation mixing initial and recurrent events overestimates performance and a naive prior-occurrence rule reaches AUROC 0.798.
abstract_snippet: "Conventional evaluation that aggregated all IDH events overestimated performance, with particularly large gaps in F1 score and AUPRC between initial and recurrent IDH predictions."
